control-plane-functional-source.description: Exact canonical hepta-control-plane snapshot, candidate routing, observability and performance aggregation implementations selected by the product control-plane surface, with executable owner tests. The standalone hepta-orchestration-kernel compatibility/experimental crate is intentionally not product evidence.

planner-functional-source.description: Exact bounded optimizer, deterministic fallback, certificate recomputation and stale-snapshot rejection implementation.

hierarchical-resource-source.description: Rust hierarchical ceiling, fairness and bounded-accounting components plus a separate durable lease journal. Tests cover local recovery; mandatory product dispatch integration and trusted terminal reconciliation remain unproved.

production-composition-source.description: Canonical ordinary service/workflow composition over the existing registry, planner, dispatch lock, CAS verifier and SQLite sequencer. Exact owner tests cover typed input binding, author/reviewer/revision, independently signed cost and commit-bound ACK, query-only recovery, cancellation and non-reexecution. Restricted research additionally requires the canonical file/replay request owner and retained trust-source currentness; a bare verified snapshot is not execution authority. Receipts, live clocks and source guards remain non-authorizing for release/submission/cutover. Local fixtures do not establish independent installed principals, provider billing, distributed revocation, complete command parity or Node retirement.

legacy-adapter-functional-source.description: Exact Node legacy adapter planning, prepared-result execution, replay, cancellation and authority-escalation rejection implementation.

scheduler-boundary-regressions-source.description: Exact Rust hard-rate arithmetic, calibration integrity, dependency-safe Pareto reduction and bounded planner regression tests.

native-state-provisioning-source.description: Native ten-database provisioning plus the exact historical 5+5 partial-root repair. The repair binds an exact read-only plan, exclusive locks on all five existing databases, restore-verified rescue, canonical construction of five missing business databases, scoped supervisor-journal repair, no-clobber publication and deterministic crash reconciliation. These source paths remain non-authorizing: online writer activation, target-host qualification and Node retirement are separate. The existing offline R source-CAS publisher now preserves published results across observation failures and process crashes; exact-owner tests and the ordinary CLI exercise same-result replay without seed or tar. This bounded source path grants no installed runtime or publication authority. The offline CAS tar adapter now uses the existing bounded process-group owner with opt-in full stdout capture, unchanged listing/description caps, restricted child environment and ordinary CLI cancellation. Unverified cleanup retains the unpublished stage; cancellation after publication retains committed bytes for the original replay path. This does not qualify tar identity, hostile same-UID containment, kernel I/O preemption, installed migration or publication authority. Archive-controlled member names follow an option terminator; cancellation, timeout and unknown-cleanup classes survive DESCRIPTION extraction as well as listing. Actual CLI fixtures cover both phases and an option-like member name. The same native maintenance bundle also owns offline store-migrate: original embedded SQL, one exclusive requested-range transaction, locked history/lease checks, retained-descriptor receipt hashing, hot-journal refusal and explicit postcommit uncertainty. Its actual CLI, Node comparison and subprocess/crash tests do not supply installed writer fencing or authority.
